New Delhi: Press Club of India president Sangeeta Barooah Pisharoty on Saturday said the journalists’ body neither organised nor endorsed the ‘Modi Chalisa’ event at its premises, calling it “a victim of a breach of trust”.Sharing a video statement on X, Pisharoty said the Press Club regularly rents out its premises and has a standard operating procedure (SOP) governing such events.“By now several of you may have noticed a photograph or a video clip featuring certain individuals reciting what they call the Modi Chalisa at the Press Club of India. At the outset, I want to reiterate clearly that that event was neither organized by the Press Club of India nor it endorsed it. A clear no,” she said.The clarification came after photographs and videos from Thursday’s event were widely circulated online, showing a cutout of Prime Minister Narendra Modi being depicted in a god-like manner as a devotional poem described as the ‘Modi Chalisa’ was recited. The Press Club had issued a clarification the same day, stating that it had not organised the event and that club authorities stopped it after the terms of the venue booking were violated.Pisharoty said the club’s rules require every event to be recommended by a member, who must also be present during the programme.“In this case, the trust placed by the club on the recommending member was breached,” she said, adding that the member was not present during the event, which was itself a violation of club rules.She said the hall had been booked for a press conference, but the organisers instead lit a live fire indoors.“Instead a live fire was lit indoors inside the hall which was a huge violation of the terms under which our venue is rented out,” Pisharoty said, adding that the secretary general has also issued show-cause notices to those concerned and initiated a review of the SOPs, she said.The organiser, Rajan Singh, vice-president of the Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board, told PTI that he planned to construct a temple for Modi in Bihar.“For the first time ever, Prime Minister Narendra Modi ensured that the transgender community gets its rights... If we want to construct a temple for him, what is wrong with it?” Singh said.He said the proposed temple for “Lord Shri Narendra Modi ji” would cost Rs 112 crore and be built on five acres of land in Bihar.Pisharoty, meanwhile, said the Press Club would continue to focus on media freedom and open discussion.“The Press Club of India has always stood for the rights and freedoms of journalists,” she said, adding that the Managing Committee was committed to “preserving and carrying forward that legacy”.
Article Summary: Press Club of India president Sangeeta Barooah Pisharoty on Saturday said the journalists’ body neither organised nor endorsed the ‘Modi Chalisa’ event at its premises. The clarification came after photographs and videos from Thursday’s event were widely circulated online, showing a cutout of Prime Minister Narendra Modi being depicted in a god-like manner.

Article Title: Assam achieves historic milestone with IVF-born indigenous Lakhimi calf: CM Sarma
Article Text:
The world’s first IVF female calf of the Lakhimi breed - native to Assam - has been born at the Assam Veterinary and Fishery University.

GUWHATI: Assam has achieved a major milestone in livestock biotechnology with the birth of the world's first IVF-born female calf of the indigenous Lakhimi breed, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Saturday.Taking to social media platform X, Sarma described the development as a historic convergence of Assam's "Sabhyata, Sanskriti and Srijan", saying the achievement could open new avenues for the state's livestock and dairy sector."The world's first IVF female calf of the Lakhimi breed -- native to Assam -- has been born at the Assam Veterinary and Fishery University," the chief minister said.The breakthrough has been achieved at the IVF Laboratory of the College of Veterinary Science under the Assam Veterinary and Fishery University at Khanapara in Guwahati.The laboratory has been established with support under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission.The development is considered particularly significant for the conservation of Lakhimi cattle, Assam's indigenous breed, as advanced assisted reproductive technologies can help multiply genetically superior animals while preserving valuable native genetic resources.Sarma said the achievement could contribute to several areas, including indigenous breed conservation, improved disease control and higher milk productivity.In the long run, these interventions are expected to strengthen Assam's dairy economy and improve the incomes of livestock farmers."My heartiest congratulations to all the veterinary scientists and professionals behind this historic achievement," the chief minister said, adding that their work had the potential to usher in a new era for Assam's dairy sector.He described the newborn calf as small in size but significant in terms of the scientific milestone it represents for Assam's biotechnology ecosystem.The latest achievement builds on Assam's ongoing efforts to introduce assisted reproductive technologies into livestock development.Earlier this year, scientists at the veterinary college produced Assam's first IVF-born calf, a female Gir calf born in Sonapur, demonstrating the viability of embryo-transfer technology under field conditions.Scientists have said such technologies can enable faster multiplication of superior genetic stock, potentially improving milk productivity and supporting dairy farmers' incomes.The successful Lakhimi birth therefore combines modern reproductive biotechnology with the conservation of an indigenous cattle breed, giving Assam a new tool to strengthen its livestock sector.Sarma concluded his message by invoking "Gau Mata" and described the achievement as a milestone carrying significance far beyond the birth of a single calf.
Article Summary: The world’s first IVF female calf of the Lakhimi breed - native to Assam - has been born at the Assam Veterinary and Fishery University. Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma described the development as a historic convergence of Assam's "Sabhyata, Sanskriti and Srijan"

Article Title: 'Treating assembly like cinema set': MK Stalin takes dig at CM Vijay's 'conduct'
Article Text:
Stalin also accused Vijay's government of concentrating on changing the names of old schemes.

Stalin says election defeat is not permanent setback

DMK sets age and term limits for party posts

DMK redraws local organisational structure

NEW DELHI: DMK chief MK Stalin on Saturday took aim at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over his "conduct" in the state assembly, accusing the actor-turned-politician of treating the House like a film set and using it to deliver "punch dialogues".Speaking at a DMK executive meeting, Stalin also accused Vijay 's government of concentrating on changing the names of welfare schemes introduced during the DMK's previous tenure."The present chief minister is busy changing the names of all the schemes we introduced. He is treating the legislative assembly like a cinema set and delivering punch dialogues. As far as we are concerned, whether we win or lose, we are people who remain deeply connected with the day-to-day lives of the people," MK Stalin said.Stalin's remarks came as the DMK executive meeting also focused on changes to the party's organisational structure, including measures aimed at bringing more young people into key positions.Addressing the party's recent electoral defeat, Stalin said the DMK had lost an election but should not view the result as a permanent setback."Let us consider this as an opportunity we have been given to plan the future of the party.This is going to be a very important Executive Committee meeting in the history of the party. With your approval, we are going to make major and significant changes to the organisational structure of the party," said Stalin.He acknowledged that the performance of party office-bearers had contributed to the defeat and said the organisation needed to recognise its shortcomings instead of simply replacing individuals."Even if the mistake is committed by an individual, it is the 75-year-old party that suffers because of it. After a defeat, many reasons are put forward. Instead of examining each constituency individually, identifying shortcomings and simply replacing people, I decided that we need to undertake a comprehensive self-assessment," he said.The executive meeting passed a series of resolutions aimed at changing the party's organisational structure and increasing the participation of younger members.The resolutions fixed the maximum age for a Branch Committee Secretary at 45 years. The post was initially limited to two terms, although the term limit was later increased to three terms following discussions with members of the DMK Executive Committee.The party also decided to create Branch Committees in Chennai, Coimbatore, Madurai, Tiruchirappalli and Salem corporations, as well as in other corporations wherever required, to strengthen Ward Committees.In Chennai Corporation, ward committees will cover an average of 10,000 voters, while the corresponding figure will be around 5,000 voters in other corporations.For Municipal, City and Town Panchayat Ward Committee Secretaries, the maximum age has been set at 50 years, with a maximum of three terms following the revised decision.The maximum age for Town Panchayat Committee Secretaries has been fixed at 60 years, with the same three-term limit.Under the new structure, Area Committees in Chennai Corporation will cover an average of 40,000 voters, while those in other corporations will cover around 30,000 voters.The maximum age for Area Committee Secretaries has been fixed at 60 years, with a maximum of three terms.City Committees will also cover an average of 40,000 voters. Their Secretaries will have a maximum age of 60 years and a three-term limit.The party has further decided that one Union Committee should be formed for every average 30,000 voters. Union Committee Secretaries will have a maximum age of 60 years and can serve for up to three terms.The organisational changes are part of Stalin's broader effort to restructure the party following its electoral setback, with greater emphasis on youth participation, fixed tenure and a wider internal assessment of the party's functioning.
Article Summary: DMK chief MK Stalin takes aim at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He accuses Vijay of treating the House like a film set and using it to deliver "punch dialogues" Stalin also accused Vijay's government of concentrating on changing the names of welfare schemes introduced during the DMK's previous tenure.

Article Title: Bills on fast track: Over half of 18th Lok Sabha bills passed in same session, shows data
Article Text:
Parliament Bills passed without discussions

Bills passed without being on original agenda

Seven bills cleared in minutes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than half of the bills introduced in the 18th Lok Sabha so far have been passed by both Houses in the same session, with the pace of passage accelerating sharply over the past year, an analysis of data from PRS Legislative Research shows.Of the 64 bills introduced since the 18th Lok Sabha was constituted, 34, or 53%, were passed by both Houses in the session in which they were introduced.The 18th Lok Sabha initially recorded a slower pace. During the Budget Session of 2026, five of the 10 bills introduced were passed by both Houses in the same session. The pace accelerated during the Monsoon Session, which ended on August 13, with 11 of the 12 bills introduced being passed before the session concluded. The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, was the only bill left pending.The government's original legislative agenda had listed five new bills for introduction and passage and two pending bills for consideration and passage. However, six of the 11 bills eventually passed during the Monsoon Session were not included in the original agenda.Neither of the two pending bills listed for consideration and passage — the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025, and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill, 2026 — was passed.The parliamentary committee examining the VBSA Bill has not yet submitted its report, while the FCRA Amendment Bill was referred to a Joint Committee following Opposition demands for its withdrawal.The rapid passage of legislation has raised concerns over the time available for parliamentary scrutiny. PRS has previously pointed out that a short gap between introduction and passage gives MPs less time to examine proposed laws and limits opportunities for consultation with stakeholders.The Monsoon Session data illustrates the trend. According to PRS, nine of the 11 bills passed were cleared without any MP other than the minister piloting the legislation speaking on them. Seven bills were passed in five minutes or less. Held from July 20 to August 13, monsoon session had 19 sittings. Lok Sabha functioned for only 15% of its scheduled time, while Rajya Sabha worked for 33%, according to PRS.The trend towards faster passage became more visible in 2025. Three of the five bills introduced during the Budget Session of 2025 were passed in the same session, followed by eight of 13 bills during the Monsoon Session and seven of nine during the Winter Session.
Article Summary: Of the 64 bills introduced since the 18th Lok Sabha was constituted, 34, or 53%, were passed by both Houses in the session in which they were introduced. The pace of passage accelerated during the Monsoon Session, which ended on August 13, with 11 of the 12 bills introduced being passed before the session concluded.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday said the party had an "advantage" in avoiding a possible split as five members of his family are among its MPs, adding that "sometimes dynastic politics has its benefits".He suggested that even if some MPs left, the party would retain enough numbers to remain intact."Have you ever wondered why the entire party did not split? Because there are five MPs from the same family. We also have several Muslim MPs, and some staunch socialists, so our numbers would not decrease," he told news agency PTI.Yadav also sought to put to rest any speculation about the SP breaking its political alliances, saying the party had consistently stood by its commitments."The Samajwadi Party never breaks alliances. Article Title: 'Judges are not gods, won't get every judgment right': Outgoing SC Judge Sanjay Karol in farewell speech
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Retiring Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Karol in his farewell address on Saturday, said judges "are not gods and they will not get every judgment right." He also urged other judges to look beyond the facts of a case and see the person behind every litigant.The Supreme Court bid farewell to Justice Karol on his last working day, with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and senior members of the Bar, including Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and Supreme Court Bar Association president Pradeep Rai paying tribute to the outgoing judge.“We, as judges, are not gods. We will not get every judgment right. What was always in our hands was simple: to see the person, not just the petitioner. A petition can only tell you the facts of a case, but it cannot tell you what the person has already lost or what he is hoping to seek from the courts. And perhaps that is why I have always said that judging requires a certain level of humility,” Justice Karol said.“The Constitution does not ask us merely to apply the law correctly. It asks us to apply it justly. That is perhaps why the responsibility of judging has always seemed larger to me than simply deciding who is legally correct,” he added.Justice Karol, who was elevated to the Supreme Court on February 6, 2023, reflected on his nearly four-decade journey in the legal profession. He said the courtroom had never been merely a workplace for him, but a vehicle for something “greater and more important” than himself.“I will not pretend that this journey has been mine alone. This courtroom has not left me; it has supported me,” he said.Karol spent 40 years in courtrooms, initially as an advocate and later, for 19 years, as a judge. He said judges must learn to listen not only to arguments but also to the “eloquent silences” in courtrooms.“In the silence of the Bar, there is a way of listening,” he said, stressing that the judicial process was also about understanding what people were seeking “in the spaces between the words”.Recalling his first visit to Courtroom No. 1 of the Supreme Court in 1996, Justice Karol said the Bench appeared to him to be almost six feet above the ground.“Judging from there has taught me something about this courtroom's symbolism. From below, the height of the bench can appear to signify authority. From the comfort zone, it signifies something quite different, and that is responsibility with dignity and honesty,” he said.Justice Karol said the Supreme Court's true significance lay in the faith of ordinary citizens who approach it believing that someone would listen.“But we must also remember those who never reach those doors because justice is too distant, too expensive, too intimidating,” he said.Reflecting on constitutionalism and justice, Karol said concepts such as law, due process and constitutional legality could be understood through the idea of “dharma”, which he described not as ritual but as duty.“The duty of a judge is to respect justice and see that the person standing before the court, however small, however wretched, is seen and heard,” he said.Addressing the Bar, he said the principles of judging extended beyond courtrooms and judicial robes, with every individual responsible for judging their own choices, conduct and use of power.“There may be no courtrooms, no robes, no technical grounds, but in these small choices, each of us dispenses the measure of justice that we take,” he said.“A judge is a judge before he dons and after he takes off the robes,” he added.Referring to a point made by CJI Surya Kant a day earlier, Justice Karol said India had not only a living Constitution but also had to “live the Constitution”.“The greatness of our Constitution is tested not only in great cases. It is tested in ordinary conduct,” he said. Concluding his farewell address, Justice Karol said he was returning to “the most distinguished constitutional office," that of the ordinary citizen.Born on August 23, 1961, Karol studied in Shimla and obtained his law degree from Himachal Pradesh University. He became advocate general of Himachal Pradesh in 1998 and served until 2003, and was designated a senior advocate in 1999.He was appointed a judge of the Himachal Pradesh high court in March 2007 and became chief justice of the Tripura high court in November 2018. He was later transferred as chief justice of the Patna high court in November 2019 before being elevated to the Supreme Court in February 2023.
Article Summary: Retiring Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Karol said judges "are not gods and they will not get every judgment right" He urged other judges to look beyond the facts of a case and see the person behind every litigant. Justice Karol spent 40 years in courtrooms, initially as an advocate and later, for 19 years, as a judge.

Article Title: 'Will not step down': Manan Mishra reiterates stance as plea in SC seeks his removal as BCI chief

Lawyers raise welfare and fee concerns

NEW DELHI: Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman and Rajya Sabha member Manan Kumar Mishra rejected demands for his resignation, saying he holds the position through an election and represents around 25 lakh lawyers across the country.Mishra made the remarks a day after a group of lawyers from different Bar Associations in Delhi staged a protest outside the BCI office in New Delhi.The protesters raised several concerns, including Mishra's long tenure, the lack of welfare measures for advocates and the proposed increase in the enrolment fee for lawyers."I have served as the chairman of the Bar Council of India for 12 to 14 years because I was elected. Manan Mishra represents 25 lakh lawyers; he will not step down simply," Mishra said, responding to the protest.He further said: "I am an elected representative. I was neither selected nor nominated to the Bar Council of India. It is a statutory body established under the Advocates Act."The lawyers demanding his resignation also sought the implementation of an Advocate Protection Act and questioned the proposed increase in registration fees at State Bar Councils.Amid the controversy, a petition has also been filed in the Supreme Court challenging Mishra's continuation as BCI chairman. Filed by advocate Yogamaya MG through advocate Deepak Prakash, the plea alleges that his uninterrupted tenure for more than a decade is contrary to the rules governing the BCI.The petitioner has relied on Rule 12(2) of the BCI Rules, which provides for a two-year tenure for the chairman and vice-chairman, or until they cease to be members, whichever is earlier.The plea has also challenged an April 21, 2025 Gazette notification that allegedly extended Mishra's tenure until 2030. It has asked the Supreme Court to quash the notification and direct the BCI to withdraw or rescind it.According to the petition, Mishra first became BCI chairman in 2012. Although he briefly left the post in 2014, he returned as chairman in November that year and has remained in the position since then. The petitioner has claimed that his re-election in March 2025 was his seventh consecutive term.The plea has argued that the absence of a cumulative limit on repeated re-election allows the office to remain concentrated in one individual for an extended period."Although Rule 12(2) prescribes a two-year tenure, no meaningful restriction exists upon repeated re-election. Consequently, the office has remained with the same individual for nearly twelve years. Such prolonged concentration is prima facie inconsistent with the representative scheme embodied in Section 4(1)(c), under which every State Bar Council contributes to the composition of the Bar Council of India. A national institution representing the entire legal profession should not permit its highest office to remain concentrated indefinitely in one individual or a narrow regional grouping," the petition stated.The petitioner has sought Mishra's removal and fresh elections within a time-bound period under independent supervision. It has also asked for a cumulative cap on the number of years a person can serve as BCI chairman, along with a rotation system and cooling-off period to allow representatives from different states and regions to head the council.The plea has further sought an independent committee headed by a former Supreme Court judge or former chief justice of a high court. The proposed committee would be assisted by an auditor nominated by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), along with financial and technical experts.The petition has also sought an independent inquiry into the functioning and finances of the BCI Trust, "PEARL-FIRST", and the financial affairs of the All India Bar Examination.It has called for a time-bound audit of statutory funds, All India Bar Examination receipts, institutional receipts, trust finances, vendor contracts and related party transactions.As an interim measure, the petitioner has proposed an independent administrative committee to oversee the BCI if the Supreme Court orders Mishra's removal.The plea has also referred to Mishra's political role. It noted that he became a Rajya Sabha member after being nominated by the BJP in 2024.The petitioner has clarified that it is not claiming that Mishra's political affiliation alone makes him ineligible to remain BCI chairman. Instead, it has raised concerns about the combination of political office and leadership of the statutory body responsible for regulating the legal profession."Petitioner does not seek the removal of any individual merely because of political affiliation or personal disagreement with any office bearer. Nor does the petitioner invite this Court to substitute its own opinion for that of the statutory authority. The challenge is directed against structural illegality, alleged concentration of institutional control, prolonged concentration of statutory power, violation of mandatory statutory provisions governing tenure and elections, arbitrary exercise of regulatory authority, absence of transparency and accountability, and failure to preserve the representative democratic character contemplated under the Advocates Act, 1961," added the PIL.Mishra also addressed the recent controversy involving students of NALSAR University of Law in Hyderabad and the Chief Justice of India (CJI), who is also the university's chancellor."Lately, there has been a lot of irresponsible and absurd commentary circulating on social media. Students from NALSAR University, Hyderabad, decided to boycott the Chief Justice of India - who is also their Chancellor - and refused to attend the convocation ceremony where he was to preside," Mishra said."As the Chairman of the Bar Council of India, I found this deeply objectionable," he added.According to Mishra, the BCI initially issued an order stating that the enrolment of the students involved would not be processed. He said the decision was withdrawn within 15 minutes after their grievances were addressed."Within 15 minutes, that order was revoked, and the students' grievances were addressed," he said.Mishra alleged that the episode was later used by members of the Aam Aadmi Party and a group he described as the "CJP group" to demand his resignation."I have served as the Chairman of the Bar Council of India for 12 to 14 years because I was elected," he reiterated.He also said around 15 students had gathered outside the BCI office on Thursday night to demand that he step down."Yesterday, about 15 students came here at night demanding a resignation," Mishra said.Meanwhile, another group of lawyers gathered in support of Mishra and defended his position as an elected representative of the legal profession.Advocate Satyam Singh said protests alone could not remove the BCI chairman because he had been elected by members of the legal community."The BCI Chairman is an elected official who has been consistently voted into office. He hasn't been appointed through a selection process or an exam where you can simply show up and demand his resignation," Singh said."He represents 2.5 million lawyers across the country, representing them successfully for years on end," he added.On the NALSAR controversy, Singh said the issue should be viewed in the context of respect for legal institutions."The CJI is the head of the Constitution--in a sense, its guardian--while NALSAR students are future lawyers and judges who will become part of this profession, whether on the Bar or the Bench. If they do not respect or trust that institution, where does that leave us?" he said.Singh also defended Mishra's decision to issue the initial order, while acknowledging that it was subsequently withdrawn."He withdrew it and admitted it was issued in haste. However, it was necessary to send a message that one must trust and respect the institution; that was the intent behind the move," Singh said.The protest, however, was not limited to the demand for Mishra's resignation. Lawyers also raised broader concerns about welfare measures and working conditions within the profession.Advocate Raman Sharma alleged that there had been no significant nationwide welfare scheme for lawyers despite Mishra's long tenure as BCI chairman.Advocate Umesh Kumar raised the issue of a national insurance scheme for lawyers and objected to the proposed increase in enrolment fees to Rs 22,500.Other protesters, including advocate Perdeep Nagar, called for greater scrutiny of lawyers' credentials and urged the BCI to give greater attention to the welfare of members of the legal profession.
Article Summary: Bar Council of India chairman Manan Kumar Mishra rejects demands for his resignation. Mishra says he holds the position through an election and represents around 25 lakh lawyers across the country. A petition has also been filed in the Supreme Court challenging Mishra's continuation as BCI chairman.

Article Title: AICTE opens select MTech programmes to 4-year BSc graduates
Article Text:
In a communication to technical institutions and admission authorities, AICTE said the graduates could be considered only for “relevant and closely aligned” disciplines (Representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Four-year BSc (honours or honours with research) graduates may now seek admission to select ME and MTech programmes, with AICTE opening a new bridge from undergraduate science to postgraduate engineering. The move has, however, prompted calls for GATE-based admissions and limits on institutions allowed to use the route to prevent dilution of MTech standards and protect enrolment in MSc courses.In a communication to technical institutions and admission authorities, AICTE said the graduates could be considered only for “relevant and closely aligned” disciplines or specialisations in which MSc degree-holders are already eligible. It is, therefore, not a blanket opening for every BSc graduate or every MTech programme. Three-year BSc degree-holders are not covered.The decision follows the UGC’s Minimum Standards of Instruction Regulations, 2025, notified on March 26 last year, which sought to enable greater academic mobility under NEP 2020. The regulations recognise a four-year undergraduate honours or honours-with-research degree carrying 160 credits and allow graduates in relevant subjects, including physics, biology and mathematics, to enter two-year ME or MTech programmes.Until now, BE and BTech degrees have been the principal route to postgraduate engineering. MSc graduates are also admitted to select programmes in areas such as computer science, biotechnology, mathematics and applied sciences. AICTE’s decision extends that limited pathway to four-year BSc graduates without requiring them to first complete an MSc.S Vaidhyasubramaniam, vice-chancellor of SASTRA University, Thanjavur, called for tighter guardrails. “To balance PG degree enrolment in technology and science, this new policy should be implemented only in top 100 NIRF universities or top 50 engineering institutions, and admissions shall be through GATE scores only,” he said.The director of a govt engineering college, who did not wish to be named, said: “Everything is now happening under the NEP 2020 canvas and not all are correct. AICTE should also ensure that this new policy is not misused by private universities for whom AICTE approval is not necessary.”Under the framework, institutions may set minimum marks or CGPA, demand GATE or another entrance-test score, assess domain knowledge and prescribe prerequisite or bridge courses. Candidates must possess the subjects or credits required for the MTech specialisation concerned.AICTE said that academic standards must not be diluted and said the new provision would “supplement and shall not replace” the existing BE/BTech pathway. Admissions must remain within the approved intake and comply with reservation policies and other statutory requirements.The council will separately publish a discipline-wise mapping linking eligible four-year BSc courses to corresponding ME and MTech programmes. The mapping will determine the actual scale and reach of the change. It has asked institutions, universities and state and UT admission authorities to incorporate the provision in admission notifications and prospectuses.
Article Summary: Four-year BSc graduates may now seek admission to select ME and MTech programmes. AICTE opens a new bridge from undergraduate science to postgraduate engineering. Move has prompted calls for GATE-based admissions and limits on institutions allowed to use the route.

Article Title: Of funds from 19 common donors in 2024, BJP got nearly four times as much as Congress
Article Text:
AI image for representation

Business money dominates

How the number was tallied

Five donors did the heavy lifting

How commons donors contributed to two major parties

Two companies, a perfect 50:50 split

Not just BJP and Congress

How donors contributed to multiple parties

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 2024 Lok Sabha election results came as a surprise to many politicians and seasoned poll watchers alike. BJP , which had won clear majorities in 2014 and 2019, finished with 240 seats, 32 short of the halfway mark. Narendra Modi needed the support of NDA partners to form a government for a third term.When it came to political donations, however, BJP was the clear leader. India’s national parties declared ₹6,648.56 crore from 11,343 contributions above ₹20,000 in FY2024-25, according to an analysis by the Association for Democratic Reforms, or ADR. That was an increase of ₹4,104.29 crore, or 161%, over the previous financial year.BJP declared ₹6,074.02 crore from 5,522 contributions, up 171% from ₹2,243.95 crore a year earlier. Congress reported ₹517.39 crore from 2,501 contributions, an increase of 84% from ₹281.48 crore. AAP declared ₹38.11 crore, CPI(M) ₹16.96 crore and the National People’s Party ₹2.09 crore. BSP said it had received no donations above ₹20,000.Together, BJP and Congress accounted for 99.14% of the money declared by the six national parties covered by ADR. But buried inside that torrent of money was a curious crossover episode.A TOI examination of the signed FY2024-25 contribution reports submitted by BJP and Congress to the Election Commission has identified at least 19 direct donors whose Permanent Account Numbers, or PANs, appear in both filings.Together, these donors gave at least ₹258.73 crore to the two parties.The money was not divided evenly. BJP received ₹206.64 crore, or 79.87%, while Congress received ₹52.09 crore, or 20.13%. In simpler terms, of every ₹5 contributed by these common donors, roughly ₹4 went to BJP. However, the 19 donors accounted for only about 3.4% of BJP’s total declared contributions, while the corresponding figure for Congress was 10.1%.ADR classified ₹6,128.79 crore, or 92.18% of the contributions received by national parties, as coming from corporate or business sectors. Such contributions formed 94.13% of BJP’s declared total and 74.19% of Congress’s.The classification is broader than incorporated companies. It covers the corporate and business categories created by ADR from descriptions in the party filings. The biggest channel for political money was electoral trusts.ADR found that four trusts, Prudent, Progressive, AB General and New Democratic, gave national parties a combined ₹4,024.43 crore, equivalent to 60.53% of the contributions covered by its report. Prudent Electoral Trust alone gave ₹2,180.71 crore to BJP, ₹216.34 crore to Congress and ₹16.42 crore to AAP.These trust flows have been excluded from TOI’s common-donor calculation. An electoral trust pools contributions before distributing money to parties. Unless the records explicitly establish the link, a company contributing to a multi-donor trust cannot be described as having directly funded a particular party.This analysis therefore deals only with donors appearing directly in party contribution reports.TOI counted a donor as common primarily when the same PAN appeared in both filings, with the name and address used as additional checks. Where the name and PAN did not line up clearly, the amount was left out. Similar company names, group relationships or common addresses were not considered sufficient.ADR found 205 contributions worth ₹3.47 crore without declared PAN details across national parties, besides 33 contributions worth ₹38.8 lakh carrying missing or incorrect PAN information.ADR also found that BJP and Congress had not declared payment dates for their contributions. The filings establish that the money was received during FY2024-25, but do not allow every contribution to be placed precisely on the election calendar.The five largest common donors gave ₹208.5 crore, accounting for 80.59% of the ₹258.73-crore pool. The biggest was Derive Investments, a Mumbai-based investment firm. Its PAN appears against four BJP contributions adding up to ₹53 crore. Congress received another ₹5 crore from the same PAN.Next came ITC Infotech India Ltd, ITC’s wholly owned technology and digital-services subsidiary. It gave ₹33.5 crore to BJP and ₹11.5 crore to Congress, or ₹45 crore in all.ITC Ltd, the diversified conglomerate with businesses spanning FMCG, cigarettes, paperboards, packaging and agribusiness, gave another ₹39 crore to BJP and ₹4 crore to Congress. Its two-party total was ₹43 crore. ITC Ltd and ITC Infotech have been counted separately because they are separate legal entities carrying separate PANs.The fourth-largest common donor was an individual.Suresh Amritlal Kotak, a veteran cotton trader and industry figure often described by his peers as the “Cotton Man of India”, gave ₹30 crore to BJP and ₹7.5 crore to Congress, or ₹37.5 crore in all.Then came Hindustan Zinc Ltd, a Vedanta Group company and integrated producer of zinc, lead and silver. It gave ₹15 crore to BJP and ₹10 crore to Congress.Most large common donors leaned heavily towards BJP. Two companies followed a strikingly different script.Century Plyboards (India) Ltd, the Kolkata-headquartered maker of plywood, laminates and other wood products, gave ₹5 crore to BJP and ₹5 crore to Congress. Star Cement Ltd, a cement manufacturer with plants in Meghalaya, Assam and West Bengal, gave ₹3 crore to each.Micro Labs Ltd, the Bengaluru-based pharmaceutical company best known for the Dolo brand, came close to an even split, giving ₹2 crore to BJP and ₹2.05 crore to Congress.Others leaned sharply towards one party.Finolex Industries, a manufacturer of PVC pipes, fittings and resin, gave ₹5 crore to BJP and ₹1 crore to Congress. Mysore Projects gave ₹3.26 crore to BJP and ₹25 lakh to Congress.Malabar Gold Ltd, the jewellery company subsequently renamed Malabar Gold and Diamonds Ltd, gave at least ₹10.0525 crore to BJP and ₹25 lakh to Congress.Christy Friedgram Industry gave ₹1.90 crore to BJP and ₹1 crore to Congress. The other verified common donors were Russell Credit, Peoples Education Society, Sri City, Muthoot Finance, T V Mohandas Pai, Josco Fashion Jewellers and H S Purewal.Tiger Associates, a West Bengal partnership that describes itself as an area distributor for Nagaland, Sikkim and Punjab state lotteries, gave ₹60 crore to AIADMK, ₹50 crore to DMK and ₹50 crore to Trinamool Congress using the same PAN.That is ₹160 crore across three parties. Of this, ₹110 crore went to the two principal Tamil Nadu rivals, AIADMK and DMK.NATCO Pharma Ltd, a Hyderabad-headquartered pharmaceutical company focused on complex generic medicines and niche molecules, appears across five party filings.Its identified contributions total ₹35.55 crore: ₹16.5 crore to BJP, ₹10 crore to YSR Congress, ₹7 crore to TDP, ₹1.5 crore to Janasena and ₹55 lakh to CPI(M).Century Plyboards also gave ₹1 crore to YSR Congress and ₹50 lakh to TDP, taking its identified contribution across four parties to ₹11.5 crore.Vedanta Ltd, a diversified natural-resources company with operations spanning zinc, aluminium, iron ore, oil and gas, steel and power, identified political contributions of ₹67 crore to BJP, ₹25 crore to BJD and ₹20 crore to JMM in its audited standalone FY2024-25 financial statements. That was ₹112 crore across the three parties. Its broader standalone donation-expense line was ₹116 crore.Not every multi-party combination represents political rivals. BJP, TDP and Janasena contested the 2024 elections in Andhra Pradesh as NDA allies. TDP and YSR Congress, however, fought on opposite sides.Likewise, DMK and AIADMK were direct rivals in Tamil Nadu. BJP and BJD contested against each other in Odisha, while BJP and the JMM-led alliance were the principal opposing camps in Jharkhand.Deng Xiaoping famously said it did not matter whether a cat was black or white, so long as it caught mice. India’s donation filings offer their own lesson in pragmatism. For at least 19 donors, choosing between saffron and Congress blue was apparently not an either-or proposition.
Article Summary: BJP and Congress accounted for 99.14% of the money declared by the six national parties covered by ADR. The biggest channel for political money was electoral trusts. ToI counted a donor as common primarily when the same PAN appeared in both filings, with the name and address used.

Article Title: 14 yrs on, NMC still trying to update national register of docs
Article Text:
The National Medical Commission is putting forth a new proposal for mandatory re-registration of doctors across the nation.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fourteen years after the first attempt to update the national registry for doctors, the National Medical Commission has again proposed to make it mandatory for an estimated 11 lakh doctors in India to re-register through its web portal. This has been done through proposed amendments to the regulations governing registration and licensing. The last such attempt in August 2024 saw barely 32,000 doctors (3%) applying till December last year and just 1,800 (0.2%) being approved for registration.The Registration of Medical Practitioners and Licence to Practice Medicine Regulations 2023 notified in May 2023 stated that all doctors enrolled in the Indian Medical Register or any state medical register “shall update in the web portal of the Ethics & Medical Registration Board within a period of three months of publishing of these Regulation” and obtain the registration number, and a licence to practice which would be valid for five months. A year later, it was clear that it had failed spectacularly. In August last year, in response to a question in Parliament, the health ministry claimed that “application for issuance of National Medical Register (NMR) Identification (ID) is voluntary” though the regulation had clearly mandated it. The proposed amendments have removed the three-month clause and said the period would be stipulated later.Over 13.8 lakh doctors were registered in India at the end of 2025 and it is assumed that 80% of this number (over 11 lakh) would be available as many would have moved out of India, died or stopped practising.“To weed out a fraction of those in the medical register, who might not be actively practising anymore, the NMC is asking all 11 lakh doctors to re-register. Instead, the commission could just take the updated state medical council registers, run a deduplication software and reach out only to those about whom there is any confusion. For the rest, they could issue a unique identification number. They are just repeating an experiment that has already failed,” said Dr KV Babu, an ophthalmologist, one of the 32,000 who had applied through the portal.Section 30 (7) of the NMC Act 2019 states: The Ethics and Medical Registration Board (EMRB) shall ensure electronic synchronisation of the National Register and the State Register in such a manner that any change in one register is automatically reflected in the other register. Six years after the NMC was constituted in September 2020, the latest draft amendments to the 2023 regulation states that the synchronization will be done indicating that it has not been done till now.None of the fresh or updated entries in state medical registers in the past years were being automatically updated in the national medical registry.Timeline:Jul 2012- MCI Board of Governors initiate process for updating Indian Medical Register with unique numeric or alpha-numeric numberMar 2017- MCI announces proposal for all doctors to have Unique Permanent Registration Number (UPRN)May 2023- NMC’s new regulation mandating re-registration and mandating a Unique Identification (UID) Number to be generated centrally by EMRB of NMCAug 2026- Amendments to 2023 regulation- proposes making registration in national registry and new UID number valid for practice across India without having to re-register in each state
Article Summary: The National Medical Commission is putting forth a new proposal for mandatory re-registration of doctors across the nation. The last such attempt in August 2024 saw barely 32,000 doctors (3%) applying till December last year and just 1,800 (0.2%) being approved for registration.

Article Title: 'Waiting for astrologer to fix date?' Udhayanidhi Stalin challenges Vijay to prove corruption claims
Article Text:
Udhayanidhi challenges Vijay over corruption claims

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Friday challenged chief minister C Joseph Vijay to make public the alleged corruption files linked to the previous DMK government and take action if there was evidence of wrongdoing.Speaking during a debate in the assembly, Udhayanidhi responded to Vijay’s earlier remarks that he would reveal “corruption files from the previous DMK regime at an appropriate time”.During the debate, Udhayanidhi criticised Vijay’s approach and said the Assembly was not a place for cinematic rhetoric.“Don't deliver punch dialogues like in cinema in the assembly,” he told Vijay.Udhayanidhi questioned the delay in making the findings public, suggesting that the government did not have sufficient evidence to support its allegations."I urge him to open the files immediately and take action if there's solid evidence of corruption. Why is the Chief Minister hesitant to release the files? Is he waiting for his astrologer to fix the date?" Udhayanidhi added.While Vijay did not respond directly to Udhayanidhi’s remarks in the House, the state’s School education minister intervened to defend the government. The minister reiterated that Vijay was committed to transparency and would make the alleged graft files public at an “appropriate time”.The exchange led to heated arguments between DMK and TVK MLAs, with members raising slogans and briefly disrupting proceedings before the House resumed its business.The exchange comes after Vijay said on Wednesday that he had files detailing alleged corruption in three government departments and warned former DMK ministers and legislators against forcing him to “open” them. Vijay said he would make the findings public at an “appropriate time.”Earlier, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly witnessed heated exchanges on August 7 between members of the ruling TVK and the opposition DMK over allegations of corruption, fiscal management and the implementation of welfare schemes.The exchange took place during a discussion on the State Budget between former minister and DMK MLA Raghupathi and the TVK government.Highlighting the debt incurred during the previous DMK regime, Tamil Nadu Finance Minister Wilson said, "He (MK Stalin) is also responsible for the debt of Rs 1.28 lakh on the head of every citizen. They say our leader is present in the women's entitlement scheme. We say that the debt is also present in it."DMK leader and former minister Nehru defended the previous government’s borrowing, saying, "The Finance Secretary clearly stated after the Budget was presented that the government borrows money only for development purposes.""The government cannot borrow money without the approval of the Reserve Bank of India. Instead of talking about debt, look at how many schemes have actually been implemented," he added.The Assembly also passed a resolution on the same day urging the Centre to ensure an equitable and fair devolution of taxes, invoking the principle of fiscal federalism.
Article Summary: Opposition leader Udhayanidhi Stalin challenges chief minister C Joseph Vijay to make public alleged corruption files linked to the previous DMK government. Vijay said on Wednesday that he had files detailing alleged corruption in three government departments and warned former DMK ministers and legislators against forcing him to “open” them.

Article Title: 'Made-up story': Nripendra Misra rejects rift reports with Champat Rai; Ram mandir nears completion
Article Text:
Misra rejects reports of rift with Champat Rai

Most temple construction work completed

Auditorium, museum and office work in final phase

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Nripendra Misra , chairman of the Ram Mandir Construction Committee, on Friday dismissed media reports of an internal rift over the construction of the Ram temple in Ayodhya, calling the claims "completely baseless".Speaking to reporters on the final day of a three-day review meeting, Misra denied reports that former trust general secretary Champat Rai had written a nine-page letter accusing him of taking arbitrary decisions."I have not seen any such letter. Until I see the letter, I will only tell you that this is a concocted story of yours (media). There is no such letter, nor is there any such criticism, even if it were 9 pages long; he has not made any such criticism. This is merely a made-up story by you (media) people."Rai had resigned as general secretary of the trust about a month ago amid allegations of misappropriation of donations linked to the Ram Janmabhoomi temple project. His resignation had raised questions about the functioning of the trust.Misra also gave an update on the progress of the Ram temple and said most of the construction work has been completed."A review of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple construction has been conducted.In total, there are approximately 70 construction projects, out of which 60 have been completed. They have already been handed over and transferred to the Trust and the Nyas. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Trust will now oversee its maintenance. Most importantly, we will conduct an internal audit of the construction work that has been handed over to the Trust," he said.He also addressed reports of waterlogging on the temple premises during the monsoon and said work was under way to resolve the issue."Yesterday, discussions were held with both the Commissioner and the Municipal Commissioner regarding development. Due to the current rainy season, water was accumulating in the temple premises; discussions were held on how to connect it to the municipal drains. This work will be completed within two months," he informed.Misra said the focus has now shifted to completing the remaining facilities, including the auditorium, trust office and museum."There are about four months of work remaining for the auditorium and the Trust office. Yesterday, we held a meeting with the Managing Director of the Rajkiya Nirman Nigam. Today, we are visiting the museum. The main discussion is to be held on the script prepared for each gallery; the promoter company wants to show a 3D presentation according to that script and obtain approval for it. We will look into that and make a decision today," Misra added.He also highlighted that the temple project was funded entirely through donations collected by the trust and did not use government funds."The matter of greatest pride is that no government money--neither from the Central nor the State government--has been used in this. The temple was built solely from the funds collected by the Nyas."
Article Summary: Nripendra Misra rejects reports of rift with Champat Rai. Most temple construction work completed.Auditorium, museum and office work in final phase of construction. Work under way to resolve waterlogging on the temple premises during the monsoon.

Article Title: CM Dhami says government is committed to making women, youth and rural entrepreneurs self-reliant
Article Text:
Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami inaugurated Chaupal–2026 under the “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana”.

Chief minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday inaugurated Chaupal–2026 under the “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana” at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan located at the chief minister’s Camp Office. On the occasion, he said that more than 13,000 entrepreneurs across the state have so far been supported through the Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana. In addition, more than 8,000 women entrepreneurs and members of Self-Help Groups have been connected with entrepreneurship and livelihood opportunities.During the inaugural session, the chief minister announced that a state-level marketing centre would be established at 13 Gaon in IT Park, Dehradun, to facilitate the marketing of products made by Self-Help Groups from all districts of Uttarakhand.Addressing the inaugural session, the chief minister said that today, the villages of Uttarakhand are not only becoming participants in the development of the state but are also playing an important role in building a self-reliant Uttarakhand through their capabilities and hard work. He said that the enthusiastic youth and enterprising women of the state possess the desire and skills to achieve something meaningful, while Uttarakhand’s local products have immense potential to reach markets across the country and the world.What is needed is to provide the right direction to this talent.With this vision, the state government has been working to take the “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana” forward. Through the scheme, the government aims to ensure that the youth of Uttarakhand become job creators rather than job seekers. At the same time, efforts are being made to strengthen the economic condition of farmers and women. The Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana is an important means of translating this vision into reality.He said that through the scheme, rural entrepreneurs are being provided with the necessary training, financial assistance, technical guidance and support in connecting with markets to start and expand their businesses.The chief minister said that on the one hand, more than 5 lakh rural women in the state have been connected with over 70,000 Self-Help Groups through the National Rural Livelihood Mission. On the other hand, more than 3 lakh women have successfully become Lakhpati Didis. He said that the women of Uttarakhand are turning everything from hill spices, mandua (finger millet), jhangora (barnyard millet), pulses, honey, pickles and jams to handicrafts, woollen products and local art into successful enterprises.The chief minister said that the government is working to take products made in villages to major cities across the country. In this direction, an umbrella brand named House of Himalayas has been created.He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has given the nation the mantras of Vocal for Local, Local to Global and Atmanirbhar Bharat. The state government is working to translate these mantras into reality. The government wants that whenever someone purchases a product from Uttarakhand, they should also experience the hard work, culture, traditions and fragrance of the soil of the hills in that product.For this reason, facilities such as rural haats, marketing centres, collection centres and agriculture service centres are being strengthened across the state so that farmers and entrepreneurs can access better markets and receive better prices for their products.He said that a major objective of promoting rural entrepreneurship is also to check migration from the hills. The government wants young people to not be compelled to leave their villages in search of employment. Because when villages become strong, Uttarakhand becomes strong.In this direction, the government is also working through the Gramothan Project (REAP) to connect extremely poor families in villages with livelihood opportunities and increase employment opportunities in rural areas.The chief minister said that “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Chaupals” are being organised in all 13 districts of the state. The objective of these chaupals is to ensure that more and more people become aware of government schemes and are able to benefit from them. For the same purpose, publicity vans are also being sent to villages so that information about the Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana reaches the last person in society.During the programme, the chief minister felicitated Lakhpati Didis and women entrepreneurs. He also released a book and annual report prepared under the Uttarakhand State Rural Livelihood Mission. In addition, he launched the Integrated Agriculture Cluster Basic Training and Module, the Infant and Young Child Feeding Module, and the Module on Prevention and Management of Anaemia among Women and Children.Cabinet Ministers Shri Bharat Chaudhary, Shri Ganesh Joshi and Shri Khajan Das, Rajya Sabha MP Shri Naresh Bansal, MLAs Shri Umesh Sharma Kau and Smt. Savita Kapoor, Secretary Rural Development Shri Dheeraj Garbyal, and other concerned officials were present on the occasion.
Article Summary: Chief minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday inaugurated Chaupal–2026 under the “Chief Minister’s Udyamshala Yojana’ The chief minister announced that a state-level marketing centre would be established at 13 Gaon in IT Park, Dehradun, to facilitate the marketing of products made by Self-Help Groups.

Article Title: Delhi government orders construction ban for 42 days to tackle winter air pollution
Article Text:

AI cameras to monitor construction sites

What is Delhi's AI-powered Dust Portal?
